items.followUp: Calculate the concentration (% v/v) when 12 cm³ of ethanol is present in 80 cm³ of solution.

rubric.why: The percentage by volume is the volume of solute divided by the volume of solution, multiplied by 100.
rubric.description: Uses the correct % v/v relationship or substitutes the given volumes correctly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship or an equivalent substitution.

rubric.why: The given volumes produce a concentration of approximately 5.56% v/v.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for 5.56% v/v or a suitably rounded equivalent.

modelAnswer: Given: volume of acetone = 5 cm³ = 5 × 10⁻⁶ m³; volume of solution = 90 cm³ = 9 × 10⁻⁵ m³.
Formula: % v/v = (volume of solute ÷ volume of solution) × 100.

items.followUp: Write two chemical properties of non-metals.

rubric.why: Metals commonly react with oxygen to form metal oxides, which are generally basic.
rubric.description: Gives one correct chemical property of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for reaction with oxygen to form metal oxides, or another correct property with a suitable example.

rubric.why: Many metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen; some also react with water to produce hydrogen.
rubric.description: Gives a second, distinct correct chemical property of metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a distinct property, with a suitable example or equation.

modelAnswer: Metals react with oxygen to form metal oxides, which are generally basic; for example, 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO.
Many metals react with dilute acids to form a salt and hydrogen; for example, Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.

items.followUp: What are halogens? State the colours of bromine and iodine.

rubric.why: Halogens are the salt-forming non-metallic elements of Group VIIA, also called Group 17.
rubric.description: Defines halogens by their group or salt-forming nature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying them as Group VIIA/17 elements or as salt-forming non-metals.

rubric.why: Halogens have characteristic colours; for example, chlorine is greenish yellow and bromine is reddish brown.
rubric.description: Gives the correct colours of two halogens.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correctly matched halogen names and colours.

modelAnswer: Halogens are the salt-forming non-metallic elements of Group VIIA (Group 17) of the periodic table.
Chlorine is greenish yellow and bromine is reddish brown.

items.followUp: Define isotopes and describe the isotopes of chlorine using their proton and neutron numbers.

rubric.why: Isotopes have the same proton number but different neutron numbers, so their mass numbers differ.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relationship between atomic number, mass number and neutrons.

rubric.why: Protium has one proton and no neutrons.
rubric.description: Gives the proton and neutron numbers for protium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct nucleus of protium.

rubric.why: Deuterium has one proton and one neutron.
rubric.description: Gives the proton and neutron numbers for deuterium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct nucleus of deuterium.

rubric.why: Tritium has one proton and two neutrons.
rubric.description: Gives the proton and neutron numbers for tritium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct nucleus of tritium.

rubric.why: Each hydrogen isotope has one electron in the first (K) shell.
rubric.description: Shows the electron arrangement in the isotope diagrams.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for showing or stating one electron in the K shell for each isotope.

modelAnswer: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same atomic number but different mass numbers because they have different numbers of neutrons.
Diagram construction for each isotope: draw its nucleus with the proton and neutron numbers stated above, draw one K shell around the nucleus, and place 1e on that shell.
